chase: I'm sorry, but the house rules say you have to leave.
Footsteps on this old carpet are loud. I can follow those.
You went around the bookcase. Good. I'm going around it too.
I'm not fast, but I know every shortcut in the house.
The hallway loops back on itself. I've read this map twice.
I'm only one chapter behind you, but I'll catch up.
You're running in circles. I've read that page already.
Turn around, please. The gallery doesn't go anywhere else.
You're fast, but I know how this house bends.
Every door in this house creaks. I'll find you anyway.
I'm closing the gap between the shelves. Please don't panic.
You can't outrun the house. I'm sorry, but I'm faster here.
I'm right behind the bookcase now. Stay where you are, please.
I'm coming around the reading desk. Please don't go back.
I'll follow you through the lounge. You can't hide there.
Please slow down. The lounge rug is a trip hazard.
I'm not running, I'm walking very quickly after you.
The fire exit leads back to the desk. I'll wait there.
catch: This will only take a moment. Hold still for me, please.
Hold still. I'll be quick, and I won't pull hard.
I wrote your name in the lighthouse book. Please come quietly.
Got you. I'm sorry, but this is the house rule.
I have you now. Please don't fight it, it only makes it longer.
One of them is down. I'm sorry, I didn't want this.
I'm taking you back to the lounge now. Please walk with me.
Let me take your arm. I'll be gentle with it.
I'll keep my grip loose. Tell me if it hurts.
I'm only taking you to the reading room. Promise.
Almost done. I'll let go as soon as we reach the desk.
Hold still, please. Nobody here wants this to hurt.
There, I have you. The lending desk is quiet at least.
I didn't want to do that. Please don't look at me like that.
Put the flashlight down now. We're nearly at the door.
Gently now. I'll walk you back to the desk.
I'm sorry. The house rules don't leave room for argument.
Keep your hands where I can see them, please.
hear: That sounded like a door. Let me check on it.
Someone shouted down the east hallway. I'm going over there.
Something broke near the stairs. I'm going to look now.
A chair just scraped across the floor. Come on, quietly.
Footsteps behind the shelves. I'm going to check, sorry.
I heard the lounge door swing. Someone is in there.
Glass broke somewhere upstairs. I'll go see what it was.
That was a shout. I should go before it happens again.
A noise by the vents. Probably nothing, but I'll look.
Did you hear that? Something knocked on the cabinet.
A soft thud in the reading room. I'm going over now.
Something moved behind the bookcase. I'm sorry, I have to look.
I heard a door click open two floors up.
Quiet footsteps by the lighthouse book. That's a new sound.
I'll note the sound down, then go and find it.
A cart rattled in the storage room. I'm going to check.
Someone just dropped a book upstairs. I'll look.
The lounge radio clicked on by itself. Strange.
search: I lost you near the stairs. Let me check the reading room.
Nobody in the reading room. I'll try the lounge next.
I'll look behind every shelf before I go back.
I can't see you anywhere now. Maybe I should try again.
The hallway is quiet. I'll go back to my patrol route.
You slipped past me again. I'll go back and search slowly.
I'll check the lending desk, then the back rooms.
Still nothing. I'll read the map one more time.
The dust on this floor doesn't show any new prints.
I'll wait by the window and listen for you.
Maybe you went upstairs. I'll take a look.
Give me a moment to think where you'd go.
I'll go back to walking the halls. Keep quiet, please.
Nothing under the tables. I'll look in the cabinets.
I'm going back on patrol. If you move, I'll hear it.
stunned: Ow, that hurt. I'm all right, just a little dizzy.
My arm is buzzing. Give me a second to shake it off.
The shock made me drop my page. Hang on.
Everything's buzzing. I need a moment, please.
I'm not sure which way is up. Let me sit down.
That crowbar rang right through my shoulder. Ouch.
The axe knocked my balance off. I'll be standing soon.
You stunned me. That was very effective, honestly.
My hands are still tingling. Give me a minute.
I dropped the book. I'll pick it up in a moment.
I'm recovering. The room is spinning a little, that's all.
Right, I'm up. My legs are still a bit wobbly.
The shock is fading. I'm not angry, just surprised.
I'll sit here until my vision clears. Please wait.
Ouch. That stung more than it should have.
hide_spot: You're in the locker, aren't you? I can see your shoe.
Under the bed, I think. Let me check, sorry.
The cabinet door is shut. Should I open it?
There's a shape in the corner. Hello there.
You can't hide under a blanket that small, you know.
I'm going to peek inside the locker. Please stay quiet.
Nice spot, but the cupboard creaks when people breathe.
I'll walk past this bed. Don't move, please.
The wardrobe is too neat. Somebody's hiding inside.
I'm checking the locker now. I'm sorry in advance.
Behind the curtain? I've read that trick before.
I'll walk right past you, so hold your breath.
I can see the curtain moving. Come out, please.
I'm opening the cupboard now. Please don't scream.
You're very good at this. I'd still find you, though.
light: Oh, your flashlight just found me. That was rude, but okay.
You're holding the flashlight on me again. I can feel it.
Please turn that light away. It makes it hard to think.
Your light is in my eyes again. Please, just a second.
Careful with the flashlight. You'll wake up the whole house.
I can't read with that thing pointed at my face.
That beam is very bright. I'm seeing spots now.
Please lower it a little. I can't see the page at all.
I'm blinking. Give me one moment, please.
All that light and I still lost my bookmark.
Your flashlight is a bit much for a quiet hallway.
Please point it at the floor. My eyes need a break.
The beam makes every word on this page disappear.
You've got me in the light. I'll step back, sorry.
Bright light again. I'm going to squint at you now.
idle: I'm on chapter nine. Please don't spoil it for me.
Reading out loud helps me think. Forgive the noise, please.
The lending cards are on the table. Take one if you like.
The line cards always come back in the same order. Nobody set it.
I filed the new arrival under strange, in the lighthouse book.
Every book in this house has a bookmark. Even the sad ones.
I read this same paragraph six times. It still won't get shorter.
I mark my favorite lines with a pencil, very lightly.
Would you like a lending card? Just write your name on it.
Nothing on the shelves today. I'll finish my chapter instead.
The reading lamp hums softly. I like that sound.
I'm sorting the cards by color again. Don't mind me.
Quiet hours are my favorite. The house sounds like paper.
I could read all night, if the house let me.
The dust on the top shelf is older than me, I think.
ability: Shine it on my arms, and the whole floor starts listening.
Light my arms and the rest of the house starts searching.
Each burst pushes your exposure up. I wish I didn't have to.
Once the bursts finish, I go quiet and wait again.
Light me once and every hunter here gets more likely to find you.
A second flash doesn't restart my count. Let the first one finish.
Ten seconds, then fifteen, then twenty. I always count them.
The house has a rule: lit up means noticed. I wrote that down.
Three bursts is the rule for each flash. I didn't make it.
I don't enjoy the bursts. They're the part I wish I could skip.
I'm sorry, the house wants everyone to know where you are.
Now the others can all feel where you're standing. I'm sorry.
When you light me up, the house hears about it soon.
That's three bursts, five seconds apart. Please try not to panic.
mechanic: Please don't run down the stairs. The third step creaks.
Stay near the desk. The others come through the side door first.
The side door sticks, so push it twice.
The vent above the lounge leads straight to the lending desk.
The lift needs its relay back before it will move. Check the panel.
The radar is blinking near the stairs. Someone is close.
Dropping from the balcony hurts, so take the stairs instead.
Pull the red book and the bookshelf slides aside.
I'll cover the lounge door. Keep the others on the far side.
Who left the chairs stacked in the hall again? That's the third time.
There's a key under the lending desk. I put it there.
The elevator is still dead. Somebody should look at the relay.
Don't climb the shelves. They tip over and make a terrible noise.
If you hit the vent grate, I'll hear it from here.
I left the sign on the door. It says the reading room is closed.
The side door needs a push before it opens. Twice, I think.
Batteries are in the lending drawer. Please don't take them all.
The relay panel is behind the desk. I'll show you.
